The Treatment

What It Is

Anti-Wrinkle Injections are a prescription treatment. Small amounts of a muscle-relaxing medicine are injected into specific facial muscles, which softens the lines those muscles make when they contract.

They work on dynamic lines, the ones caused by movement, such as frowning or raising your brows. Lines that are visible when your face is completely still, or that come from loss of volume or sagging skin, may need a different treatment or a combination.

Whether the treatment suits you, and which areas are worth treating, is decided by the doctor at an in-person consultation.

Book a consultation

Uses

What It Is Used For

Expression Lines

  • Forehead lines: horizontal lines from raising the brows.
  • Frown lines: the vertical lines between the brows.
  • Crow's feet: lines at the outer corners of the eyes when you smile.
  • Bunny lines: small lines on the sides of the nose.

Shaping and Other Uses

  • Brow lift: a small lift at the tail of the brow.
  • Gummy smile: less gum showing when you smile.
  • Jaw slimming: relaxing an enlarged chewing muscle (masseter).
  • Excessive underarm sweating (hyperhidrosis).

Not every area suits every face. The doctor will tell you if a treatment is unlikely to give the result you are hoping for.

Safety

Before You Decide

Possible Side Effects

Redness, swelling or a small bruise where the needle went in are the most common effects, and they are temporary. Less often, the medicine affects a nearby muscle and causes a temporary droop of an eyelid or brow. The doctor will go through the risks with you before treatment.

When It May Not Be Suitable

Treatment is usually avoided during pregnancy and breastfeeding, with an infection where the injection would go, with certain nerve and muscle conditions, or with a known allergy to the product. Some medicines matter too, so bring a list of what you take.

Questions

Common Questions

Didn't see yours? Ask it on WhatsApp before you book.

Ask a question
What do Anti-Wrinkle Injections treat?

Lines caused by muscle movement, such as forehead lines, frown lines between the brows and crow's feet. Lines that are visible when your face is completely still, or that come from loss of volume, may need a different treatment.

Are the results permanent?

No. The effect wears off gradually as the muscle activity returns, so treatment is repeated if you want to keep the result. The doctor will explain what to expect in your case.

Will my face look frozen?

The aim is to soften lines, not to stop all expression. Talk to the doctor about the look you want at your consultation.

Is it the right treatment for my lines?

It depends on what is causing them. Lines from movement respond best. Lines from volume loss or sagging skin may suit other treatments, such as Dermal Fillers, which the clinic also offers.
